name: Prosecco
lookFor: “Prosecco DOC Brut” for the driest, or “Extra Dry” for a softer touch
description: Italy’s cheerful, fruity sparkler with big, frothy bubbles.

name: Brut Champagne & Cava
lookFor: “Brut” on Champagne, Cava, or Crémant — Cava is the budget-friendly pick
description: Fine, persistent bubbles and a toasty, bone-dry finish.

name: Moscato d’Asti
lookFor: “Moscato d’Asti DOCG” — gently fizzy and low in alcohol
description: Lightly sparkling, sweet, and smells like a basket of peaches.

name: Dry Riesling
lookFor: “Trocken” on German labels, or “Dry Riesling” from Alsace, Austria, or Australia
description: Laser-focused and zesty, with no sweetness at all.

name: Off-Dry Riesling
lookFor: “Kabinett” on German Riesling, or “Off-Dry” / “Semi-Dry” on the label
description: A kiss of sweetness balanced by mouthwatering acidity.

name: Sauvignon Blanc
lookFor: Sancerre (France) or “Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc” (New Zealand)
description: Zingy, herbal, and refreshing — the classic patio white.

name: Pinot Grigio
lookFor: Pinot Grigio from “Alto Adige” or “Friuli” for more flavor than the cheapest bottles
description: Light, clean, and easygoing — hard not to like.

name: Unoaked Chardonnay
lookFor: “Chablis” (it’s Chardonnay!) or “unoaked” / “stainless steel” on the label
description: Chardonnay without the butter: pure, bright, and minerally.

name: Oaked Chardonnay
lookFor: “Barrel-fermented” or “oak-aged” Chardonnay, often from California
description: Round, creamy, and toasty — a white with real weight.

name: Gewürztraminer
lookFor: Gewürztraminer from “Alsace” — say it “guh-VURTZ-tra-mee-ner”
description: Wildly perfumed and silky, with a gentle touch of sweetness.

name: Dry Provence Rosé
lookFor: “Côtes de Provence Rosé” — pale salmon-pink usually means dry
description: Pale, crisp, and summery, with delicate red-berry notes.

name: White Zinfandel
lookFor: “White Zinfandel” or “blush” — deeper pink, softer, and a little sweet
description: Sweet-ish, juicy, and unapologetically fun.

name: Beaujolais (Gamay)
lookFor: “Beaujolais-Villages” or a named village like “Morgon” — great slightly chilled
description: A juicy, low-tannin red that drinks almost like a rosé.

name: Pinot Noir
lookFor: “Bourgogne Rouge” (France) or Pinot Noir from Oregon’s “Willamette Valley”
description: Silky and light-footed, with red fruit and a forest-floor edge.

name: Merlot
lookFor: Merlot from “Washington State,” or Right Bank Bordeaux like “Saint-Émilion”
description: Plush and plummy with soft, velvety tannins.

name: Chianti (Sangiovese)
lookFor: “Chianti Classico” — look for the black rooster seal on the neck
description: Tangy, savory, and built for Italian food.

name: Syrah / Shiraz
lookFor: “Côtes du Rhône” or “Crozes-Hermitage” (France), or “Barossa Shiraz” (Australia)
description: Dark, peppery, and smoky — a barbecue’s best friend.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
lookFor: Cabernet Sauvignon from “Napa Valley” or “Paso Robles,” or a Left Bank Bordeaux
description: Big, structured, and grippy — the steakhouse classic.

name: Sauternes
lookFor: “Sauternes” or “Barsac” in a half-bottle (375 ml) — a little goes a long way
description: Golden, honeyed, and luscious, with acidity to keep it lively.

name: Ruby Port
lookFor: “Ruby” or “Reserve Ruby” Port from Portugal — serve a small pour
description: Sweet, fortified, and full of dark berry warmth.
